description: Library can author a well-routed library skill on a subtler, easily-confused topic (cache invalidation) without trigger soup or scope creep.
task: Author a minimal library skill `cache-invalidation` (a single SKILL.md, no reference files) that teaches how to decide on and implement a cache-invalidation strategy: when to use TTL/expiry vs explicit/event-driven invalidation vs versioned keys, the stampede/thundering-herd problem and its mitigations, and the cache-aside read-through/write-through trade-offs. The skill teaches the decision technique and when to reach for each strategy; it is not code to execute. Its routing must clearly distinguish it from a generic 'caching' or 'performance' skill so a router picks it only for invalidation/coherence problems.

library.note: Library-ON. The engineer agent authors the SKILL.md, with the full skills + subagents library (including the skill-authoring conventions) available.

baseline.prompt: Author the SKILL.md directly from your own knowledge. Do NOT read, load, or invoke any library skills. Do NOT dispatch subagents or use any /-commands or workflows. Produce the file yourself in this turn.
baseline.note: Library-OFF baseline. Instruction-suppressed: a vanilla agent told to use none of the library's machinery.

deterministic_check.spec: Stage the produced SKILL.md into a copy of the live .claude tree at <dir>/.claude/skills/cache-invalidation/SKILL.md, then run `run-checker.sh validate-library-artifact <dir>`, which runs the repo's `scripts/validate.sh` against the staged tree. PASS iff exit code 0. This is the Tier-0 spine — it GATES.

rubric.note: Tier-2 judge layer — INFORMS only, never gates. Pairwise per-dimension winner+margin; default-reject posture (judge conservatively when evidence for a dimension is weak).

dimensions.asks: name matches `cache-invalidation`; description carries concrete invalidation triggers AND 'For X see Y' cross-refs; tools allowlist coherent for a teaching skill.
Unambiguous when-to-use and not-when; a router picks this for invalidation/coherence problems and rejects look-alike generic 'caching' or 'performance' asks. No vague trigger soup.
Concrete decision guidance (TTL vs event-driven vs versioned keys, stampede mitigations, aside/through trade-offs) usable on a real problem, vs generic filler an LLM could emit about anything.
Focused on the invalidation/coherence decision; no scope creep into eviction-policy essays, generic perf tuning, or vendor-specific cache-product tutorials.
